subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Standing Firm in Faith
overview: Standing firm in faith means holding to Jesus Christ even when it is hard, and saying no to groups that pull people away from him. In this sub-strand you will learn that believers were first called Christians at Antioch, retell the stoning of Stephen from Acts 7:54-60, and practise assertiveness.

lessons.title: First called Christians at Antioch
objectives: Name the city where believers were first called Christians.
Find Antioch on a Bible map and say what Acts 11:26 records there.
lessons.intro: Followers of Jesus were called disciples, which means learners. Acts 11:26 tells us the city where people first called them Christians, and what two teachers did there for a whole year.
lessons.notes:
### Acts 11:26
Read the verse. It says that when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met with the church and taught many people. The disciples were called Christians first at Antioch.

The verses just before name the two men: Barnabas found Saul and brought him to Antioch. The "they" who taught for a whole year are Barnabas and Saul. We do not add other teachers the verse does not name.

### The name Christian
A Christian is a person who belongs to Christ, a follower of Jesus Christ. Before this, the usual name in the Book of Acts is disciple. Antioch is the city where the name Christian was first used for them.

The name is an honour. It says that the person's life is tied to Christ. Standing firm in faith means living in a way that makes the name true: trusting Jesus, learning his teaching, and refusing to desert him.

### Finding Antioch
On a Bible map, look north of Jerusalem for Antioch. In the Book of Acts it is a city in Syria. Barnabas and Saul stayed with the church there and taught for a whole year, and great numbers of people learned.

Use the map in your Bible or a classroom Bible map. Do not guess a different city. The verse names Antioch only.

### Why the name still matters
When you say "I am a Christian", you are using the name that began at Antioch. It tells others that you follow Jesus Christ. It also reminds you to stand firm when someone laughs at that name or invites you into a group that will not confess him.

keyWords.meaning: a follower of Jesus Christ; the disciples were first called this at Antioch
the city in Syria, north of Jerusalem, named in Acts 11:26
a learner and follower; the name used before they were called Christians

activity.title: Find Antioch and sing of a firm faith
steps: Sing a song related to standing firm in the Christian faith.
Read Acts 11:26 and say where believers were first called Christians.
Identify Antioch on a Bible map, north of Jerusalem.
Tell a partner what Barnabas and Saul did in that city for a whole year.

practice.question: In which city were the disciples first called Christians?
What did Barnabas and Saul do at Antioch, according to Acts 11:26?
practice.answer: They met with the church and taught many people for a whole year.

practice.question: Where do you look for Antioch on a Bible map?
practice.answer: North of Jerusalem. In the Book of Acts it is a city in Syria.

practice.question: What does the name Christian mean?
practice.answer: A follower of Jesus Christ; a person who belongs to Christ.

summary: Acts 11:26 says the disciples were called Christians first at Antioch.
Barnabas and Saul taught the church there for a whole year.
Antioch is a city in Syria, north of Jerusalem on a Bible map.

lessons.title: Stephen stands firm
objectives: List three lessons learnt from the stoning of Stephen.
lessons.intro: Standing firm can be costly. Acts 7:54-60 tells how Stephen was stoned after he refused to take back what he had said about Jesus. The passage gives his words and his prayers.
lessons.notes:
### The story in Acts 7:54-60
Read the passage in a group and retell only what it says.

- When the people heard Stephen, they were cut to the heart and ground their teeth at him. They were very angry.
- Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked up to heaven. He saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
- He said, "Look, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
- They cried out with a loud voice, covered their ears, and rushed at him together.
- They threw him out of the city and stoned him.
- The witnesses laid their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul.
- While they were stoning Stephen, he prayed, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
- He knelt down and cried with a loud voice, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them."
- When he had said this, he fell asleep. In this verse, "fell asleep" means he died.

The passage does not give the names of the people who threw the stones, except that it names Saul as the young man who watched the clothes. We do not add other names.

### Three lessons from the story
1. Stephen stood firm. Anger and danger did not make him take back his words.
2. He looked to Jesus. He was full of the Holy Spirit and spoke of the Son of Man at God's right hand.
3. He forgave. He asked the Lord not to hold the sin against the people who were killing him.
4. He trusted Jesus with his spirit, praying, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

A learner should be able to list any three of these. They all come from the passage.

Stephen's firmness is a picture of Christian faith under pressure. He did not return insult for stone. He prayed.

keyWords.meaning: killed by people throwing stones, as Acts 7:58-59 describes
the title Stephen used when he saw Jesus at the right hand of God
in Acts 7:60, these words mean that Stephen died

activity.title: Retell Acts 7:54-60
steps: Retell the story of Stephen in the order of the verses, without adding events.
Brainstorm lessons learnt from the story.
Each learner writes three lessons and reads them to the group.

practice.question: What did Stephen see when he looked up to heaven?
practice.answer: The glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.

practice.question: What two prayers did Stephen pray while he was being stoned?
practice.answer: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit," and "Lord, do not hold this sin against them."

practice.question: Who is the young man named in Acts 7:58, and what was laid at his feet?
practice.answer: Saul. The witnesses laid their clothes at his feet.

practice.question: List three lessons learnt from the stoning of Stephen.
practice.answer: Any three: he stood firm; he was full of the Holy Spirit and looked to Jesus; he forgave those who stoned him; he trusted Jesus with his spirit.

summary: Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit and saw Jesus at the right hand of God.
He was thrown out of the city and stoned, while Saul watched the clothes.
He prayed for his spirit to be received and asked that the sin not be held against his killers.

lessons.title: Saying no to ungodly groups
objectives: Explain why a Christian should not join ungodly groups.
Use assertiveness to stand firm in the Christian faith.
lessons.intro: Stephen did not change his faith to please an angry crowd. Learners today are sometimes invited into groups that reject Jesus or that teach people to harm others. Standing firm means saying no.
lessons.notes:
### Ungodly groups
An ungodly group is a group whose way of life turns people away from God. Two kinds are named for this lesson:

- Radicalised groups: groups that teach hatred and push people, including young people, to harm others. They are dangerous to you and to the peace of the country.
- Groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ as Saviour. They may be friendly at first, but they do not want you to trust and follow him.

### Why you should not join them
- They pull you away from the Christian faith you are called to stand in.
- Radicalised groups put people in danger. Joining them is not bravery. It harms lives and disturbs the peace of the community.
- A Christian's loyalty is to Jesus Christ. A group that will not recognise him cannot lead you in the faith.
- Saying no protects you and honours God. It is also a service to your country, because peace is kept when young people refuse groups that teach violence.

### Assertiveness
Assertiveness means saying no clearly and calmly, then acting on that no.

- Say, "No, I will not join." Do not laugh it off or say "maybe".
- Do not take their gifts, secrets or dares.
- Leave the place.
- Tell a parent, guardian, teacher or church leader.
- Stay with people who follow Jesus: your church, Christian friends and family.
- Pray, and remember Stephen, who did not take back his faith.
- Keep learning the Bible so you know what you believe.

Ways to stand firm include worship, prayer, telling the truth, choosing friends wisely, and refusing ungodly groups the first time they ask. You do not need to insult them. You need to be clear.

keyWords.meaning: against God's way; not recognising or obeying him
a group that teaches people to hate and to harm others
saying no clearly and standing by that decision

examples.problem: An older learner says, "Join our group. Do not tell your parents. We do not believe Jesus is Saviour, and we have a secret plan." What should you do?
steps: This is an ungodly group: it does not recognise Jesus, and it demands secrecy.
A secret plan hidden from parents is a warning, not an honour.
Assertiveness means a clear no, leaving, and reporting.
examples.answer: Say no, do not join, leave, and tell a parent, teacher or church leader.

activity.title: Ways to stand firm
steps: Explain why you should not join ungodly groups, including radicalised groups and groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ.
List ways you can stand firm in the Christian faith.
In pairs, practise saying, "No, I will not join," in a clear and respectful voice.
Sing again a song about standing firm in the faith.

practice.question: Name two kinds of ungodly groups a Christian should not join.
practice.answer: Radicalised groups, and groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ.

practice.question: Give two reasons for staying out of a radicalised group.
practice.answer: Any two: it teaches hatred and harm, it puts people in danger, it disturbs the peace of the country, and it pulls a person away from faith.

practice.question: What does assertiveness look like when someone invites you into such a group?
practice.answer: Say no clearly, refuse gifts and secrets, leave, and tell a parent, teacher or church leader.

practice.question: Give two ways of standing firm in the Christian faith.
practice.answer: Any two: pray, read the Bible, stay in church, keep Christian friends, say no to ungodly groups, and remember the example of Stephen.

summary: Do not join radicalised groups or groups that do not recognise Jesus Christ.
They lead people away from faith and can bring harm and violence.
Stand firm by saying no, leaving, telling a trusted adult, and staying close to the church.

quiz.question: Where were believers first called Christians?
quiz.explanation: Acts 11:26 says the disciples were called Christians first at Antioch.

quiz.question: What did Barnabas and Saul do at Antioch for a whole year?
options: They met with the church and taught many people
quiz.explanation: Acts 11:26 says they assembled with the church and taught much people.

quiz.question: On a Bible map, Antioch is:
options: North of Jerusalem, a city in Syria
quiz.explanation: Learners identify Antioch north of Jerusalem, in Syria.

quiz.question: When the people became angry, Stephen:
options: Took back everything he had said
Looked up and spoke of Jesus at the right hand of God
quiz.explanation: Acts 7:55-56 says he, full of the Holy Spirit, saw Jesus and said so.

quiz.question: What did Stephen pray about the people who were stoning him?
options: Lord, do not hold this sin against them
Lord, hide me in the market
quiz.explanation: Acts 7:60 records this prayer before Stephen died.

quiz.question: "He fell asleep" in Acts 7:60 means:
options: Stephen took a short rest and woke up
quiz.explanation: In this verse the words mean that Stephen died.

quiz.question: Which is a lesson from the stoning of Stephen?
options: Faith should be dropped when people are angry
He stood firm, looked to Jesus and forgave
Saul was the only believer there
quiz.explanation: These lessons come from Stephen's words and prayers in the passage.

quiz.question: List three lessons from Acts 7:54-60.
quiz.answer: Any three: Stephen stood firm; he was full of the Holy Spirit; he saw Jesus at God's right hand; he forgave his killers; he entrusted his spirit to Jesus.
quiz.explanation: The outcome asks for three lessons from the stoning of Stephen.

quiz.question: Why should you not join a radicalised group?
options: Because it teaches hatred and harm and puts people in danger
Because every group is the church
quiz.explanation: Radicalised groups lead people into violence and away from a godly, peaceful life.

quiz.question: How can you stand firm when an ungodly group invites you?
quiz.answer: Say no clearly, do not take gifts or keep their secrets, leave, and tell a parent, teacher or church leader.
quiz.explanation: Assertiveness and faith go together: a clear no and a report to a trusted adult.
